recentItems.title: Extreme heat forces Rhone winemakers to harvest early
recentItems.description:
(31 Aug 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Serrières, France - 27 August 2026
1. Aerial view of the Boissonnet estate vineyards
2. Various of grape harvest
3. SOUNDBITE (French) Guillaume Boissonnet, winemaker at Domaine Boissonnet:
“The 2026 vintage is a very sunny one, with vines that struggled throughout the season. However, vines over 15 to 20 years old withstood the conditions very well. We have a truly promising, very healthy harvest.”
4. Various of grape harvest
5. Close of grape
6. SOUNDBITE (French) Guillaume Boissonnet, winemaker at Domaine Boissonnet:
“It is quite impressive how well the vines have held up this year. We are looking at a high-quality harvest with very respectable yields, and you can see that the grapes have really soaked up the sun, they have turned a beautiful golden colour.”
7. Various of vines

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mauves, France - 27 August 2026
8. Aerial view of the Coursodon estate
9. Various of grape harvest
10. SOUNDBITE (French) Jérôme Coursodon, winemaker at Domaine Coursodon:
“I started in 1998; back then, the harvest usually took place around September 15th or 20th. We had an early warning in 2003 with an exceptional vintage, we started on August 16th. Since 2003, we’ve started in late August on four or five occasions. This year, we are approaching the situation we saw in 2003. When it comes to climate change, it is up to us to adapt, and we realize we need to find the right balance. Currently, we aren't seeing very high alcohol levels. We are aiming for equilibrium, around 13% or 13.5%, because consumers no longer want wines with high alcohol content, and the fruit expression is also better at around 13%.”
11. Various of grape harvest
12. Close of grapes
STORYLINE:
A pair of secateurs closes on a bunch of Marsanne, and the grapes drop into a bucket already warm from the morning sun.

This is Serrières, on the steep right bank of the Rhône, and the harvest is under way in August. Domaine Boissonnet began picking on the 18th.

"The 2026 vintage is a very sunny one, with vines that struggled throughout the season. However, vines over 15 to 20 years old withstood the conditions very well. We have a truly promising, very healthy harvest," says Guillaume Boissonnet, who runs the estate.

The heat that pulled the calendar forward also kept the vineyard clean, a welcome benefit.

"Thanks to the weather conditions, we had absolutely no issues with powdery or downy mildew, nor any rot, so the grapes were able to ripen under good conditions," says Boissonnet.

He splits a grape between his fingers to check the flesh.

"It is quite impressive how well the vines have held up this year. We are looking at a high-quality harvest with very respectable yields, and you can see that the grapes have really soaked up the sun — they have turned a beautiful golden colour," he says.

What is happening in Saint-Joseph is happening across the country. After a historically hot, dry spring, 2026 is shaping up as one of the earliest harvests France has recorded, with some southern vineyards cutting their first grapes in mid-July.

A few kilometres downstream, at Mauves, the slopes pitch up sharply. 

The Coursodon estate farms some of the appellation's steepest hillsides, terraces where everything is carried by hand. A team of about fifteen pickers works the rows.

Jérôme Coursodon measures the change against his own career.


Heat concentrates sugar in the grape, and sugar becomes alcohol in the vat. Left unchecked, hotter summers push wines ever stronger. 

Adapting, for him, means picking at the right moment to hold the balance.

recentItems.title: China MOFA briefing highlights
recentItems.description:
(31 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Beijing, China -  31 August 2026
Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun

1.Do you have any updates on the ongoing rescue efforts for the Gyirong mudslide disaster? 

The Chinese government has provided Nepal with emergency cash assistance and humanitarian aid. The first batch of 50 tons of disaster relief supplies has already arrived in Kathmandu, and two batches of rescue teams composed of Chinese tunnel rescue experts have rushed to the front lines of the disaster-hit areas in Nepal. We have also shared important information with the Nepalese side, including imagery, satellite and hydrological data from the disaster-hit areas, as well as early warning information on the barrier lake upstream. We are actively assisting stranded Nepalese citizens in returning to Nepal as soon as possible.
As of noon yesterday, all Chinese nationals who had been reached in the disaster-hit areas of Nepal had been properly evacuated and accommodated, and they were in a safe condition. 
At present, China is making every effort to search for and rescue people from both China and other countries who remain unaccounted for, while maintaining close communication with foreign embassies in China to jointly conduct checks on missing foreign nationals and properly handle follow-up matters.

2.Some Indian TV channels have blamed China for the floods and mudslide disaster. They said China ignored warnings from scientists and is going ahead with major construction projects and hydropower infrastructure. Would the ministry like to comment on this? 

We noted that experts from China and Nepal have reached some assessments about the cause of the disaster. According to their analysis, the disaster was triggered by the collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal. In the face of major disasters, we firmly oppose such groundless and malicious speculation.

3.It appears that China has censored and taken down some of the more dramatic videos of the terrible flood smashing into Gyirong port. Why has China done that? Also, there have been some suggestions by particularly Tibetan groups outside China that the number of missing and dead is understated. What are China's responses to the accusations?

At present, the search and rescue of the personnel and other disaster relief work at the site are being carried out intensively and in an orderly manner. China releases information in an open, transparent and timely manner. Making malicious smearing and hyping on the disaster is unpopular. 

4.More than 900 people are believed to be stuck inside a blocked hydropower project tunnel in Nepal after the flood last week. Were there any Chinese nationals working on this project, and has the government identified any of those who are Chinese nationals trapped in the tunnel? 

Nearly a hundred Chinese nationals remain missing in disaster-hit areas in Nepal. Nepal is making utmost efforts to search and rescue those missing and trapped. Tunnel experts from China have arrived at the site to assist with the relevant rescue and search.

5.US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the world cannot allow China to have a $1.2 trillion trade surplus and that the G20 should revisit its trade terms with China. What is the Foreign Ministry’s comment?

China-US economic and trade relations are mutually beneficial and win-win in nature. China has never deliberately pursued a trade surplus and opposes unilateral tariff measures in all forms. We stay committed to high-standard opening up and will leverage China's large market to provide new opportunities for all parties, including the US.

recentItems.title: Mira cómo se limpia el esqueleto de un enorme anfibio de 240 millones de años de antigüedad
recentItems.description:
(31 Aug 2026) 
SOURCE - RESTRICTIONS
LOCATION - DATE SHOT

Slug: Evergreen Polonia Esqueleto de anfibio SP
Source: ASSOCIATED PRESS
 
AP video shot by: Rafal Niedzielski
 
Mira cómo se limpia el esqueleto de un enorme anfibio de 240 millones de años de antigüedad
__________________________________________

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Varsovia, Polonia - 21 de julio de 2026 

Fue uno de los anfibios más grandes que jamás haya habitado la Tierra, un temible depredador acuático de los albores de la era de los dinosaurios.
 
Hoy, este fósil de 240 millones de años permanece atrapado en la roca en el Centro de Ciencias Copérnico de Varsovia.
 
Más de 2.000 voluntarios se turnan para retirar cuidadosamente el material circundante.
 
El fósil mide más de seis metros de longitud.
 
Una vez finalizada la restauración, este Mastodonsaurus será el ejemplar más grande expuesto en un museo del mundo.
 
SOUNDBITE (polaco) Tomasz Sulej, Instituto de Paleontología de la Academia Polaca de Ciencias:
“Hace dos años encontramos este enorme esqueleto. Estábamos muy contentos, pero no sabíamos qué hacer con él”, comenta este paleontólogo.
 
++Partes superpuestas con video de voluntarios trabajando++

SONIDO (polaco) Tomasz Sulej, Instituto de Paleontología de la Academia Polaca de Ciencias:
“Desde hace ya muchos meses, voluntarios de toda Polonia acuden para tocar este fósil, este esqueleto de un animal que vivió hace 240 millones de años, y para utilizar punzones para extraerlo de la roca, muy lenta y cuidadosamente”, explicó.
 
El Mastodonsaurus vivió durante el periodo Triásico Medio.
 
Era un depredador de emboscada acuático que se alimentaba principalmente de peces y anfibios más pequeños.
 
SONIDO (polaco) Tatyana Kozyk, coordinadora de los equipos de voluntarios:
++Partes Superpuestas con imágenes de video++ 
“ha estado esperando tantos años y soy yo quien lo toca y lo descubre. A día de hoy, todavía me cuesta asimilarlo”, dijo esta coordinadora de voluntarios.
 
Desde 2025, los voluntarios se han inscrito a través del sitio web del Centro de Ciencias Copérnico para sumarse a esta iniciativa, y la institución sigue invitando a otras personas.
 
SONIDO (polaco) Dorota Serafin, voluntaria:
++Partes superpuestas con video++
“Vivimos en el siglo XXI, rodeados de tecnología a diario; por eso, la oportunidad de tocar la prehistoria, una época que ninguno de nosotros recuerda y sobre la que sabemos muy poco, es verdaderamente extraordinaria”, dijo esta voluntaria.
 
ANNE MARIE GARCIA, ASSOCIATED PRESS

recentItems.title: Helicopters with supplies and search teams come and go from Nuwakot army camp in Nepal
recentItems.description:
(31 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++PLEASE NOTE: THE EDIT HAS BEEN EXTENDED TO ADD SHOT #7++

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot district, Nepal - 31 August 2026
1. A helicopter lands at Nuwakot army camp
2. Pan from military personnel to a helicopter landing
3. Mid of military personnel getting out of a helicopter 
4. Zoom out of officials getting our of a helicopter, inspecting supplies
5. Wide of a helicopter taking off
6. Mid of military personnel closing a helicopter's doors and walking away
7. Various of people getting off helicopter
STORYLINE:
Multiple foreign teams were assisting local rescuers Monday to find workers stuck in tunnels at Nepal's power plants on the rivers that flooded last week. 

Military and emergency workers were loading and unloading helicopters with aid as rescuers were trying to find trapped workers in at least a dozen hydroelectric plant sites Monday.

Last week's catastrophic flooding in Nepal and Tibet killed at least 900 people and left more than 4,700 missing.

The president of the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal, Mohan Kumar Dangi, said the floods damaged at least 12 hydropower projects across Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts and about 900 people were missing from the project sites.

Officials have previously offered varying estimates of the number trapped.

Nepal’s disaster agency said Monday that 903 deaths had been counted in that country, with 4,247 people, including 592 foreigners, missing. As of Sunday, Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, and Chinese state media said 261 of the missing were foreigners, including over a hundred Nepalis.

AP video shot by Rishi Lekhi

recentItems.title: Palestinian rapper performs to a massive crowd in Damascus for the first time
recentItems.description:
(31 Aug 2026) 
SYRIA PALESTINIAN RAPPER CONCERT

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY: NO ACCESS YOUTUBE 

LENGTH: 1:42

++NIGHT SHOTS++

ASSOCIATED PRESS  - NO ACCESS YOUTUBE
Damascus, Syria -  28 August 2026
1. Various of crowd singing along with Palestinian rapper who goes by the stagename BiGSaM
2. BiGSaM performing on stage
3. Crowd singing along with BiGSaM
4. Various of BiGSaM performing on stage
5. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) BiGSaM, Palestinian rapper:
“Being in Damascus for the first time signifies a very important moment for me personally. It’s a dream I’ve had for a long time and it has finally come true.”

6. Crowd singing along and filming BiGSaM with their phones
7. Woman filming Big Sam while he performs
8.  SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Paloma Touma, concert goer: 
“I have been listening to BiGSaM for a long time, we love him a lot. We came all the way from Tartous. We drove for three hours to see him, and it was very much worth it.” 

9. BiGSaM performing on stage, with Palestinian and Syrian flags, and wearing the keffiyeh, a checkered scarf that has come to embody Palestinian solidarity
10. Woman wearing the Palestinian keffiyeh in the crowd singing along
11. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) BiGSaM, Palestinian rapper:
“I believe that we are all one nation, not two. The Palestinian people are the Syrian people, we have always spoken with the same voice, we even sing with the same voice.” 

12. Various of people at concert, music playing
STORYLINE:
Thousands of people packed a Damascus venue on Thursday night for a Palestinian rapper's first performance in Syria, chanting along to his songs and dancing throughout the concert. 

Outside, roughly twice as many people waited to get a glimpse into the show, which sold out.

Palestinian rapper BiGSaM's music has built a following across the Arab world, but the night marked a personal milestone for him.

“Being in Damascus for the first time signifies a very important moment for me personally. It’s a dream I’ve had for a long time and it has finally come true,” he said.

His concert came as the Syrian capital sees renewed cultural and musical activity following the fall of President Bashar Assad in December 2024. 

Some musicians and artists who had spent years away from the country have returned to perform, while a new, young generation of Syrians has begun gathering again around concerts.

But BiGSaM's arrival in Damascus carried a different significance because much of his following as a Palestinian artist had grown through recordings and social media. 

On Thursday night, that digital audience turned up, becoming a physical force.

The crowd sang along to his songs almost from beginning to end, other fans held up their phones to film the show. 

The connection between the artist and his fans in Damascus was palpable during the show. 

At one point, the artists brought both a Palestinian and a Syrian flag onto the stage. 

Later, he appeared wearing a keffiyeh around his neck as the crowd continued singing along, many also donning the checkered headscarf, which has become a global symbol of Palestinian solidarity. 

The artist said the connection between Palestinians and Syrians is familial as well as cultural.

“I believe that we are all one nation, not two. The Palestinian people are the Syrian people,” he said.

The concert reflects a broader return of public cultural life to Damascus after years of war, displacement and political repression took their toll on the city’s artistic and cultural scene.



AP video by Ghaith Alsayed
Production by Malak Harb

recentItems.title: Man in Nepal lost 'everything' in flash floods 'right in front of my eyes'
recentItems.description:
(31 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Bidur, Nuwakot district, Nepal - 31 August 2026
1. Various aerials of damaged embankments of Trishuli river ++MUTE++
2. Helicopter flying overhead
3. SOUNDBITE (Hindi) Kumar (last name unavailable), flood survivor:
“I got to know only five minutes before (the floods). A yellow colored helicopter making a huge noise came close to the house and the moment I stepped out to have a look at the helicopter, I was on the top floor in the house, my mother, two sons and my wife were eating on the lower floor, when I looked at the helicopter, there was a huge noise 500 meters away from the house and I thought the helicopter has crashed. I went looking for the crashed helicopter at that moment, there was flooding. I went down, lifted my mother in my arms and asked the boys to bring along their mother. I ran towards the jungle, I must have reached at a height of just 100 meters away. I had lost everything: my house, my car, my farm. I lost them all right in front of my eyes.”
4. Various of damage
5. Various of volunteers walking
6. Aerials of damaged embankments
STORYLINE:
A survivor of Nepal's flash floods said on Monday he "lost everything", as authorities were intensifying rescue efforts after catastrophic flooding in Nepal and Tibet killed at least 900 people and left more than 4,700 missing.

"I got to know only five minutes before (the floods)," said Kumar, who survived the flood but said he lost his house, car, and farm "right in front of my eyes."

Multiple foreign teams were also assisting local rescuers to find trapped workers in hydropower tunnels. Officials say at least 90 people are trapped in multiple tunnels of hydropower plants.

Nepal’s disaster agency said Monday that 903 deaths had been counted in that country, with 4,247 people, including 592 foreigners, missing. As of Sunday, Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, and Chinese state media said 261 of the missing were foreigners, including over a hundred Nepalis.

Wednesday’s flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

AP Video shot by Rishi Lekhi and Rajesh Kumar Singh
